title: Bar private drug-industry funding for NIH, CDC and FDA regulators
proposal: The chapter says regulators at NIH, CDC and FDA should get no money from private drug companies. It says their funding should come only from the government, with oversight from Congress.
quote: All National Institutes of Health, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and Food and Drug Administration regulators should be entirely free

title: Long "cooling off" period before regulators can join drug companies
proposal: The chapter calls for a long waiting period (it suggests up to 15 years) before health regulators, including FDA reviewers, can work for companies they regulated. It also says drug company executives should be limited from moving into regulatory jobs.
quote: Regulators should have a long “cooling off period” on their contracts (15 years would not be too long) that prevents them from working for companies they have regulated.

title: Measure HHS programs by health outcomes
proposal: The chapter says HHS should adopt measurements across the department that show whether its programs actually improve health and welfare outcomes, not just how much work the agency does.
quote: Finally, HHS should adopt metrics across the agency that can objectively

title: Have Congress clearly define and limit CDC's legal powers
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress clearly spell out and limit the CDC's legal authorities.
quote: Congress should ensure that CDC’s legal authorities are clearly defined and limited to prevent a recurrence of any such arbitrary and vacillating exercise of power.

title: Split the CDC into two separate agencies
proposal: The chapter recommends splitting the CDC into a data agency that must publish all the data it collects and a separate public health agency with a sharply limited ability to make policy recommendations.
quote: The CDC should be split into two separate entities housing its two distinct

title: Make CDC support, not replace, private test developers
proposal: The chapter says that in a new disease outbreak, the CDC should help private, academic and state labs develop tests by sharing information and samples, rather than making tests itself.
quote: When it comes to testing, the CDC’s role should similarly be to facilitate rather than supplant the efforts of private test developers

title: Bar CDC guidance from being treated as a requirement
proposal: The chapter says a law or rule should stop CDC guidance from telling people what they "should" do, such as masking or vaccinating schoolchildren. It says CDC should report risks and leave decisions to parents, doctors and elected officials.
quote: By statute or regulation, CDC guidance must be prohibited from taking on a prescriptive character.

title: Ban drug-company donations through the CDC Foundation
proposal: The chapter says the practice of the CDC receiving drug-company money through the nonprofit CDC Foundation should be banned.
quote: This practice presents a stark conflict of interest that should be banned.

title: Modernize public health data collection
proposal: The chapter says Congress should require HHS to collect and share health data electronically while protecting privacy. It also says HHS should partner with a private data expert to build a real-time information system.
quote: HHS should also enter into a public–private partnership with a data-management expert to develop a system

title: Move vaccine safety monitoring from CDC to FDA
proposal: The chapter recommends moving the CDC's vaccine safety programs (VAERS, the Vaccine Safety Datalink and the CISA Project) and their funding to the FDA.
quote: Those functions and their associated funding should be transferred to the FDA, which is responsible for post-market surveillance

title: End CDC programs seen as not respecting life; study abortion risks
proposal: The chapter says the CDC should end programs that do not respect human life, conscience rights or family formation, stop promoting abortion as health care, and fund studies on the risks of abortion.
quote: The CDC should eliminate programs and projects that do not respect human life and conscience rights and that undermine

title: Ban research using cells or tissue from abortions
proposal: The chapter says research that uses cells or tissue from aborted fetuses should be prohibited by law and policy. Later it adds that Congress should ban abortion-derived fetal tissue research altogether.
quote: and aborted baby body parts can easily be provided by alternative sources. All such research should be prohibited as a matter of law and policy.

title: Update CDC messaging on fertility awareness methods
proposal: The chapter says the CDC should update its public messages about modern fertility awareness-based family planning methods and fund studies on them.
quote: CDC should update its public messaging about the unsurpassed effectiveness of modern fertility awareness–based methods (FABMs) of family planning

title: Push every state to report detailed abortion data
proposal: The chapter says HHS should use every tool, including cutting funds, to make each state report how many abortions occur, at what stage of pregnancy, for what reason, the mother's home state and the method.
quote: HHS should use every available tool, including the cutting of funds, to ensure that every state reports exactly how many abortions take place within its borders

title: Require reporting of abortion complications and born-alive cases
proposal: The chapter says the CDC should require monitoring and reporting of complications from abortion and of every case of a child born alive after an abortion.
quote: CDC should require monitoring and reporting for complications due to abortion and every instance of children being born alive after an abortion.

title: Tie Medicaid family planning money to state abortion reporting
proposal: The chapter points to the Ensuring Accurate and Complete Abortion Data Reporting Act, which would require states to report abortion data on time as a condition of federal Medicaid family planning payments.
quote: would amend title XIX of the Social Security Act and Public Health Service Act to improve the CDC’s abortion reporting mechanisms

title: Stop CDC collection of gender identity data
proposal: The chapter says the CDC should immediately stop collecting data on gender identity.
quote: The CDC should immediately end its collection of data on gender identity

title: Stop drug makers from delaying first generic versions
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should stop drug companies from holding onto, without using, their legal right to be the first to sell a generic version of a drug.
quote: the FDA should prohibit pharmaceutical companies from purposely sitting on their legally available right to be the first to sell generic versions of their drugs.

title: Help generic makers get samples; curb delaying petitions
proposal: The chapter says Congress should give generic drug companies legal ways to get samples of brand-name drugs and should ban meritless "citizen petitions" used to delay generic approval.
quote: Congress should create legal remedies for generic companies to obtain samples of brand-name products for their generic development efforts

title: Let labs share lab-developed tests more easily
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should create ways for laboratory-developed tests to be shared with other labs without the current regulatory burdens.
quote: the FDA should introduce mechanisms through which laboratory-developed tests can easily be shared with other laboratories

title: Ease rules for "laboratory-modified" tests
proposal: The chapter says laws and rules should be revised to make it easier to use modified versions of existing medical tests.
quote: the applicable statutes and regulations should be revised to facilitate greater access to such modified tests.

title: Sort out overlapping FDA and CMS authority over lab tests
proposal: The chapter says Congress, the FDA and CMS should clarify and separate their overlapping authority over medical tests.
quote: Congress, the FDA, and the CMS need to clarify and disentangle overlapping authorities over tests to eliminate regulatory confusion.

title: Grade drug factories and label drugs with facility codes
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should replace pass/fail factory inspections with a graded system and put facility codes on drug packages with a searchable database, so buyers can favor reliable makers.
quote: The FDA should also add facility codes to drug packaging and construct a searchable database that cross-references product codes and facility codes.

title: Exempt multi-source generic drugs from Medicaid rebates
proposal: The chapter says HHS should exempt generic drugs made by several companies from having to pay rebates to Medicaid and other federal health programs.
quote: HHS should exempt multi-source generic drugs from requirements to pay rebates to Medicaid and other federally funded health programs

title: Promote trials of new uses for generic drugs
proposal: The chapter says the FDA and NIH should encourage studies testing new uses for generic drugs, possibly with NIH funding or running them.
quote: FDA and NIH should promote efficacy trials of new applications for generic drugs

title: Reverse FDA approval of abortion pills
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should reverse its approval of chemical abortion drugs such as mifepristone, arguing the approval process was illegal.
quote: Reverse its approval of chemical abortion drugs because the politicized approval process was illegal from the start.

title: Restore in-person dispensing rules for abortion pills
proposal: As a first step, the chapter says the FDA should bring back its stricter safety rules (REMS) on abortion pills to end telehealth and mail-order distribution.
quote: As an interim step, the FDA should immediately restore the REMS by removing the in-person dispensing requirement to eliminate dangerous tele-abortion and abortion-by-mail distribution.

title: Bring back pre-2016 limits on mifepristone
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should restore earlier mifepristone rules, including a 49-day pregnancy limit, in-person dispensing, and reporting of all serious side effects, and apply them to generic versions.
quote: A bare-minimum policy of limiting abortion pills to the pre-2016 policy of 49 days gestation, returning to the pre-2021 in-person dispensing requirement

title: Improve reporting of abortion pill complications
proposal: The chapter says the FDA's adverse event reporting system should be fixed so that hospital and emergency room workers report abortion pill complications, and reporting should be made quicker and easier.
quote: Address weaknesses in the current FAERS (FDA Adverse Events Reporting System). The Administration and policymakers should ensure that health care workers

title: Disclose FDA inspections of abortion pill makers
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should be open about inspections of abortion pill sponsors and factories and answer congressional and public records requests on time.
quote: Implement a policy of transparency about inspections of the abortion pill’ s sponsors, Danco and GenBioPro, as well as facilities that manufacture the pills.

title: Stop approving mail-order abortion pills
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should stop promoting or approving mail-order abortion pills, citing federal laws on mailing abortion drugs.
quote: Stop promoting or approving mail-order abortions in violation of long-standing federal laws that prohibit the mailing and interstate carriage of abortion drugs.

title: Restore waiver to import vaccines not linked to fetal cells
proposal: The chapter says the FDA should restore a waiver letting doctors import certain Japanese-made vaccines in bulk for patients with religious objections.
quote: The FDA should restore the waiver to comply with RFRA and for the obvious public health benefits of increased childhood vaccination

title: Require drugs made without fetal cell lines
proposal: The chapter says the FDA and NIH should require drugs and biologics to be developed with cell lines that do not come from aborted fetuses.
quote: the FDA and NIH should require the development of drugs and biologics that are free from moral taint and switch to cell lines

title: Tighten rules on drug advertising
proposal: The chapter says the FDA or Congress should more strictly regulate where and how drug companies advertise, especially on media outlets.
quote: The FDA or Congress should regulate where and how paid advertising is used by pharmaceutical companies more stringently, especially on media outlets.

title: Restore ethics board for fetal tissue research
proposal: The chapter says HHS should quickly bring back the ethics advisory committee that reviews research using tissue from abortions.
quote: Promptly restore the ethics advisory committee to oversee abortion-derived fetal tissue research

title: End NIH in-house fetal tissue research and stem cell registry
proposal: The chapter says NIH should end its own research projects that use tissue from abortions and close its human embryonic stem cell registry.
quote: End intramural research projects using tissue from aborted children within the NIH, which should end its human embryonic stem cell registry.

title: Fund alternatives to embryo and fetal tissue research
proposal: The chapter says HHS should fund other research methods so that research relying on abortion or destroying embryos becomes obsolete.
quote: Aggressively implement a plan to pursue and fund ethical alternative methods of research

title: Reconvene a National Council on Bioethics
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should bring back a National Council on Bioethics to study new ethical questions in research and health policy.
quote: the Administration should reconvene a new National Council on Bioethics (NCB) to discuss new and emerging areas of ethical concern

title: Ban three-parent embryo and human cloning research
proposal: The chapter says research that creates three-parent embryos and human cloning research should be banned.
quote: because every child has a right to a mother and father, three-parent embryo cre-ation and human cloning research should be banned.

title: Create a research agenda on harms of abortion
proposal: The chapter says HHS should create and promote research that supports pro-life policies and looks at mental and physical harms of abortion to women and girls.
quote: HHS should create and promote a research agenda that supports pro-life policies and explores the harms, both mental and physical

title: Term limits for top NIH career leaders
proposal: The chapter says top career (non-political) leaders at NIH should have term limits.
quote: The NIH monopoly on directing research should be broken. Term limits should be imposed on top career leaders at the NIH

title: Consider block-granting NIH research money to states
proposal: The chapter says Congress should consider giving NIH's grant budget to states as block grants so they can fund their own research.
quote: Congress should consider block granting NIH’s grants budget to states to fund their own scientific research.

title: Shut down the CDC and NIH Foundations
proposal: The chapter says the CDC Foundation and NIH Foundation, whose boards include drug company executives, should be shut down.
quote: The CDC and NIH Foundations, whose boards are populated with pharma-ceutical company executives, need to be decommissioned.

title: Abolish NIH diversity office and panel gender quotas
proposal: The chapter says NIH should stop requiring a certain number of women on conference panels and should abolish its Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion.
quote: the NIH Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion, which pushes such unlawful actions, should be abolished.

title: Fund studies on harms of gender transition treatments
proposal: The chapter says NIH should fund studies on the short- and long-term negative effects of gender transition treatments for young people.
quote: it should fund studies into the short-term and long-term negative effects of cross-sex interventions

title: Restore Trump-era Medicare rules and pilot programs
proposal: The chapter says the next Administration should bring back Trump-era Medicare rules and pilot programs that were dropped or weakened, including MCIT, RADV, MAQI and the direct contracting model.
quote: The next Administration should reintroduce and restore regulations and demonstrations from the Trump Administration that were withdrawn, weakened, or never finalized

title: Pay the same for Medicare services regardless of setting
proposal: The chapter says Medicare should pay the same for a service whether it is done in a doctor's office, clinic or hospital, including ending the inpatient-only list and adding procedures for surgery centers.
quote: CMS should expand the application of site-neutral payment options to more settings.

title: Restore conscience protections for medical workers
proposal: The chapter says HHS should restore and strengthen conscience rules so health workers in federal programs are not forced to provide sex-change or similar services.
quote: HHS needs to restore and enhance conscience protection regulations that allow medical practitioners to participate in federal health care programs

title: Lift limits on physician-owned hospitals
proposal: The chapter says Congress should remove Affordable Care Act limits so physician-owned hospitals can serve Medicare patients.
quote: These restrictions should be removed so that physician-owned hospitals can compete with other hospitals in serving Medicare patients.

title: Make Medicare Advantage the default for new enrollees
proposal: The chapter says Medicare Advantage (private plans) should be the default choice when people join Medicare, and beneficiaries should directly control how they spend Medicare dollars.
quote: Make Medicare Advantage the default enrollment option. 2. Give beneficiaries direct control of how they spend Medicare dollars.

title: Use competitive bidding to pay Medicare Advantage plans
proposal: The chapter says Medicare Advantage should switch from a formula-based payment model to competitive bidding, along with changing risk adjustment and removing some plan rules and benefit limits.
quote: Replace the complex formula-based payment model with a competitive bidding model.

title: Shift traditional Medicare to value-based payments
proposal: The chapter says legislation should replace traditional Medicare's fee-for-service system with value-based payments and base payments on patient health or service intensity rather than location.
quote: Replace the bureaucrat-driven fee-for-service system with value-based payments to empower patients to find the care that best serves their needs.

title: Write price transparency into law; redirect 340B drug subsidies
proposal: The chapter says Congress should make health price transparency rules permanent law and restructure the 340B drug discount program to benefit patients rather than hospitals.
quote: Restructure 340B drug subsidies27 toward beneficiaries rather than hospitals.

title: Repeal Medicare Shared Savings Program and Inflation Reduction Act
proposal: The chapter says legislation should repeal health policies such as the Medicare Shared Savings Program and the Inflation Reduction Act.
quote: Repeal harmful health policies enacted under the Obama and Biden Administrations such as the Medicare Shared Savings Program

title: Repeal Medicare drug price negotiation
proposal: The chapter says the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug price negotiation program should be repealed. Until then, it says the law should be carried out in a way that limits its effects.
quote: This “negotiation” program should be repealed, and reforms in Part D that will have meaningful impact for seniors should be pursued.

title: Change Medicare Part D cost sharing
proposal: The chapter says Part D reforms should end the coverage gap, lower the government's share of costs in the catastrophic tier, and make drug makers pay a larger share.
quote: Other reforms should include eliminating the coverage gap in Part D, reducing the government share in

title: Change Medicaid funding to block grants or per-person caps
proposal: The chapter says Medicaid financing should change to give states more flexibility, using options such as a blended match rate, block grants, overall caps or per-person caps.
quote: This system should include a more balanced or blended match rate, block grants, aggregate caps, or per capita caps.

title: Replace Medicaid expansion's enhanced federal match
proposal: The chapter says CMS should replace the higher federal match rate (used for the Medicaid expansion) with a different rate, end state financing loopholes, and reform hospital payments, including Disproportionate Share Hospital payments.
quote: Replace the enhanced match rate with a fairer and more rational match rate.

title: Reward states for fighting Medicaid fraud
proposal: The chapter says states that do more to cut waste, fraud and abuse in Medicaid should get extra payments and higher federal matching for fraud and eligibility systems.
quote: An enhanced contingency fee should be paid to states that successfully increase their efforts to decrease waste, fraud, and abuse.

title: Tighten Medicaid eligibility checks and asset tests
proposal: The chapter says CMS should hold states responsible for wrong eligibility decisions, require stronger eligibility checks, and strengthen asset tests.
quote: Hold states accountable for improper eligibility determinations. b. Require more robust eligibility determinations. c. Strengthen asset test determinations within Medicaid.

title: Let families use Medicaid money for outside coverage
proposal: The chapter says CMS should launch a "personal option" letting families use Medicaid dollars to buy coverage outside Medicaid.
quote: CMS should launch a robust “personal option” to allow families to use Medicaid dollars to secure coverage outside of the Medicaid program.

title: Allow Medicaid work requirements
proposal: The chapter says CMS should make clear that states can adopt work requirements for able-bodied adults on Medicaid and charge premiums and cost sharing to higher-income enrollees.
quote: Add work requirements and match Medicaid benefits to beneficiary needs.

title: Allow time limits or lifetime caps on Medicaid
proposal: The chapter says CMS should allow targeted time limits or lifetime caps on Medicaid benefits.
quote: Add targeted time limits or lifetime caps on benefits to disincentivize permanent dependence.

title: Let states put Medicaid money toward private insurance
proposal: The chapter says Congress should let states help pay for private insurance for whole families through flexible accounts, including catastrophic plans paired with HSA-like accounts.
quote: Congress should allow states the option of contributing to a private insurance benefit for all members of the family in a flexible account

title: Let states cut Medicaid benefit mandates without waivers
proposal: The chapter says CMS should let states drop outdated benefit requirements and, for able-bodied enrollees, mandates that go beyond private insurance, and redesign long-term care to focus on the truly needy.
quote: CMS should add flexibility to eliminate obsolete mandatory and optional benefit requirements

title: Reduce Medicaid waiver and state plan approval steps
proposal: The chapter says CMS should let payment reforms happen without lengthy waivers or state plan amendments where possible, and give states more control of Medicaid management.
quote: CMS should allow providers to make payment reforms without cumbersome waivers or state plan amendment processes where possible.

title: Clarify direct primary care is not insurance for HSAs
proposal: The chapter says rules should make clear that a direct primary care subscription fee is not insurance, so it works with health savings accounts.
quote: Changes should clarify that DPC’s fixed fee for care does not constitute insurance in the context of health savings accounts.

title: Replace No Surprises Act dispute process
proposal: The chapter says the No Surprises Act's payment dispute process should be scrapped and replaced with a truth-in-advertising approach.
quote: The No Surprises Act should scrap the dispute resolution process in favor of a truth-in-advertising approach

title: Allow shared savings and reference pricing plans
proposal: The chapter says CMS should make sure insurance designs that reward patients for choosing lower-cost care are allowed.
quote: CMS should ensure that shared savings and reference pricing models that reward consumers are permitted.

title: Separate subsidized and unsubsidized ACA insurance markets
proposal: The chapter says CMS should plan to separate the unsubsidized insurance market from the subsidized ACA exchange market and free it from costly ACA rules.
quote: To make health insurance coverage more affordable for those who are without government subsidies, CMS should develop a plan to separate the non-subsidized insurance market

title: Add quality measures to hospital price transparency
proposal: The chapter says future updates of hospital price posting rules should include quality measures.
quote: Future updates of these rules should focus on including quality measures.

title: Write expanded short-term, association plans and HRAs into law
proposal: The chapter says Congress should make permanent the expansion of association health plans, short-term health plans and health reimbursement arrangements.
quote: by codifying an expansion of association health plans, short-term health plans, and health reim-bursement arrangements (including individual coverage HRAs)

title: Expand access to health savings accounts
proposal: The chapter says CMS's insurance office should work with Treasury and OMB to expand access to health savings accounts.
quote: to give consumers more flexibility with their health care dollars through expanded access to health savings accounts.

title: Loosen lab testing personnel rules (CLIA)
proposal: The chapter says CMS should revise lab rules (CLIA) on what clinical labs and testing staff are allowed to do.
quote: CMS should similarly revise CLIA rules regarding scope of practice for clinical laboratories and testing personnel.

title: Let research labs qualify to do clinical testing
proposal: The chapter says CMS should create a way for non-clinical labs and researchers to gain the equivalent of CLIA certification for clinical testing.
quote: CMS should create pathways for granting non-clinical laboratories and their testing personnel CLIA certification equivalency.

title: Withdraw Medicaid guidance on abortion travel
proposal: The chapter says HHS should withdraw Medicaid guidance and related waivers that could help pay for travel for abortions, and the DOJ Office of Legal Counsel should withdraw its opinion that this does not violate the Hyde Amendment.
quote: Two of the first actions of a pro-life Administration should be for HHS to withdraw the Medicaid guidance (and any Section 1115 waivers issued thereunder)

title: End federal funding of Planned Parenthood and abortion providers
proposal: The chapter says taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers should end. It says HHS should tell states they can defund Planned Parenthood and should propose a rule to remove abortion providers from Medicaid.
quote: Policymakers should end taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood and all other abortion providers and redirect funding to health centers

title: Pass the Protecting Life and Taxpayers Act
proposal: The chapter says Congress should pass the Protecting Life and Taxpayers Act to cut off federal funding to abortion providers such as Planned Parenthood.
quote: Congress should pass the Protecting Life and Taxpayers Act,50 which would accomplish the goal of defunding abortion providers

title: Approve state waivers excluding abortion providers from Medicaid
proposal: The chapter says CMS should act on pending waivers from Idaho, South Carolina and Tennessee that seek to bar abortion providers from their Medicaid programs.
quote: CMS should resolve pending Section 1115 waivers from Idaho, South Carolina, and Tennessee

title: Withhold Medicaid funds from states requiring abortion coverage
proposal: The chapter says HHS should withhold funds, up to 10 percent of Medicaid money, from states that require insurance to cover abortion, citing the Weldon Amendment, and DOJ should defend those decisions in court.
quote: HHS/CMS should withdraw appropriated funding, up to and including 10 percent of Medicaid funds, from states that require abortion insurance coverage.

title: Require truly separate payments for ACA abortion coverage
proposal: The chapter says HHS should bring back a Trump-era rule requiring insurers to collect a separate payment for abortion coverage in ACA plans, and make the charges truly separate.
quote: HHS should reinstate a Trump Administration regulation and enforce what the plain text of Section 1303 requires.

title: Audit HHS compliance with the Hyde Amendment
proposal: The chapter says HHS should do a full audit of compliance with the Hyde Amendment and similar funding limits, including the Biden Administration's post-Dobbs actions.
quote: HHS should undertake a full audit to determine compliance or noncompliance with the Hyde amendment

title: Rescind EMTALA emergency abortion guidance
proposal: The chapter says HHS should rescind 2022 guidance saying emergency-care law can require abortions, end related investigations, and have DOJ drop its lawsuits against pro-life states on this issue.
quote: HHS should rescind the guidance and end CMS and state agency investigations into cases of alleged refusals to perform abortions.

title: Reissue Medicare decision on gender surgery coverage
proposal: The chapter says CMS should reissue its 2016 decision not to set a national Medicare coverage rule for gender reassignment surgery, and state that evidence does not support such coverage.
quote: CMS should repromulgate its 2016 decision that CMS could not issue a National Coverage Determination (NCD) regarding “gender reassignment surgery”

title: Investigate cases of infants born alive after abortion
proposal: The chapter says HHS should use EMTALA and disability law to investigate cases of infants born alive after abortion and left untreated, and revive a Trump-era proposed rule for this purpose.
quote: HHS should revive a Trump Administration proposed regulation, “Special Responsibilities of Medicare Hospitals in Emergency Cases

title: Pass the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act
proposal: The chapter says Congress should pass this act to require medical care for infants who survive an abortion and set criminal penalties for practitioners who do not provide it.
quote: In addition, Congress should pass the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act

title: Make Hyde and Weldon abortion funding limits permanent law
proposal: The chapter says Congress should permanently write the Hyde amendments and Weldon Amendment protections into law, through bills like the Conscience Protection Act, which would also let victims sue in court.
quote: Permanently codify both the Hyde family of amendments and the protections provided by the Weldon Amendment.

title: Reverse redefinition of sex in HHS nondiscrimination rule
proposal: The chapter says the definition of sex discrimination that includes gender identity, sexual orientation and abortion should be reversed in all HHS and CMS programs, including CHIP, by restoring the Trump-era Section 1557 rule.
quote: The redefinition of sex to cover gender identity and sexual orientation and pregnancy to cover abortion should be reversed in all HHS and CMS programs

title: Keep lactation room requirements in future rules
proposal: The chapter says the lactation room requirements in the Section 1557 rule should be kept in future rulemaking or proposed in a separate rule.
quote: the lactation room requirements added in the regulation should either be consistently included in any upcoming Section 1557 rulemaking

title: Stop enforcing COVID vaccine mandate for hospitals
proposal: The chapter says CMS should announce it will not enforce the COVID-19 vaccine mandate for Medicare and Medicaid hospitals, revoke related rules, and not impose general mask mandates on health facilities.
quote: Announce nonenforcement of the Biden Administration’s COVID-19 vaccination mandate on Medicaid and Medicare hospitals.

title: Pay damages to workers fired over the vaccine mandate
proposal: The chapter says CMS should pay damages to medical workers who were fired because of the CMS COVID-19 vaccine mandate.
quote: Pay damages to all medical professionals who were dismissed directly because of the CMS vaccine mandate.

title: Apply TANF work rules to more noncash benefits
proposal: The chapter says TANF work requirements should apply to anyone getting a noncash benefit worth $50 a month for six months in a row.
quote: would apply the TANF work requirements to any noncash benefit worth $50 a month and received for six consecutive months.

title: Require states to track TANF outcomes, including marriage goals
proposal: The chapter says HHS should clarify how states track and audit TANF spending results and require measurement of goals like marriage and healthy family formation.
quote: HHS should clarify how states, in their quarterly and annual reports, ought to track and audit the outcomes

title: Fund sexual risk avoidance programs equally with other sex ed
proposal: The chapter says sexual risk avoidance (abstinence-focused) programs should get equal funding and emphasis, and teen pregnancy grants should not go to programs that promote abortion or risky behavior.
quote: SRA programs, both at ACF and at OASH and both discretionary and mandatory, should be equal in funding and emphasis.

title: Abolish approved sex-ed curriculum lists
proposal: The chapter says HHS should abolish lists of "approved" or "evidence-based" sex education curricula and instead create criteria for choosing curricula.
quote: Any lists with “approved curriculum” or so-called evidence-based lists should be abolished

title: Repeal 2016 grant rule on sexual orientation and gender identity
proposal: The chapter says HHS should repeal a 2016 rule that adds sexual orientation and gender identity nondiscrimination conditions to grants, which it says affects faith-based adoption agencies.
quote: should repeal the unnecessary 2016 regulation61 that imposes nonstatutory sexual orientation and gender identity nondiscrimination conditions on agency grants

title: Pass the Child Welfare Provider Inclusion Act
proposal: The chapter says Congress should pass this act so adoption and foster care providers cannot face discrimination because of their beliefs about marriage.
quote: Congress should pass the Child Welfare Provider Inclusion Act62 to ensure that providers and organizations cannot be subjected to discrimination

title: Move the Office of Refugee Resettlement to DHS
proposal: The chapter says the Office of Refugee Resettlement should be moved from HHS to the Department of Homeland Security.
quote: The Office of Refugee Resettlement should be moved to the Department of Homeland Security.

title: Transfer care of migrant children to DHS and end Flores
proposal: The chapter says Congress should change the trafficking law to move all care of unaccompanied migrant children to DHS and end the Flores settlement agreement.
quote: to transfer all ORR duties for unaccompanied alien children to DHS and eliminate the Flores settlement agreement.

title: Bar abortions for minors in refugee office custody
proposal: The chapter says ORR should withdraw its policy allowing elective abortions for children in its care and tell care providers not to transport girls for elective abortions.
quote: ORR should withdraw its policy of allowing elective abortions for children in ORR care

title: Create a child support tax credit
proposal: The chapter says tax law should be changed so lower-income parents who pay child support can get a child support tax credit similar to the earned income tax credit.
quote: tax law should be updated to ensure that nonresident parents with child support orders can receive a nondependent, child support tax credit.

title: Encourage state child support payment apps
proposal: The chapter says states should be encouraged to set up easy smartphone apps for paying and tracking child support, including informal support.
quote: Each state should be induced to implement a high-tech, easy-to-use application to cen-tralize child support payments.

title: Use marriage education funds for high school curricula
proposal: The chapter says Healthy Marriage and Relationship Education grants should pay for state high school lessons on healthy marriage, sexual risk avoidance and relationships.
quote: Utilize HMRE funding or grants to provide state-level high school education resources and curriculum on healthy marriages

title: Allow child abuse prevention funds for marriage education
proposal: The chapter backs a recommendation that Congress make clear child abuse prevention grants can pay for marriage and relationship education.
quote: Congress could change the law to make it clear that Title II funding can be used for healthy marriage and relationship education.

title: Have Title X clinics share information on marriage
proposal: The chapter says HHS should require Title X family planning clinics to tell clients about the importance of marriage and refer them to marriage resources.
quote: HHS should require clinics it funds under Title X (family planning) to provide information to customers about the importance of marriage

title: Keep marriage grants open to faith-based groups
proposal: The chapter says marriage and fatherhood grants should protect and prioritize faith-based groups, including those that define marriage as between one man and one woman.
quote: HMRE program grants should be available to faith-based recipients who affirm that marriage is between not just any two adults, but one man and one unrelated woman.

title: Run a national pro-fatherhood messaging campaign
proposal: The chapter says fatherhood program funds should support national campaigns affirming the role of fathers and offering relationship education.
quote: HMRF funds should be used to support national messaging campaigns that affirm the role fathers play in the lives of their children

title: Speed termination of parental rights in some foster cases
proposal: The chapter says ACYF should fund programs that promote father involvement, and where a parent makes no serious effort to be involved, parental rights for children in foster care should be ended quickly.
quote: does not make a sincere or serious effort to be involved in the child’s upbringing, termination of parental rights for children in foster care should be swift.

title: Eliminate Head Start
proposal: The chapter says the Head Start preschool program and the entire Office of Head Start should be eliminated. At minimum, it says Head Start's COVID-19 vaccine and mask requirements should be rescinded.
quote: Given its unaddressed crisis of rampant abuse and lack of positive outcomes, this program should be eliminated along with the entire OHS.

title: Make sure aging programs do not encourage assisted suicide
proposal: The chapter says the Administration for Community Living should review its programs to make sure they support palliative care and do not facilitate physician-assisted suicide.
quote: HHS ACL should survey their programs to ensure that they are supporting vulnerable persons of age or disability and are not facilitating or encouraging participation in PAS.

title: Revise the national family caregiver strategy
proposal: The chapter says the National Strategy to Support Family Caregivers should be reexamined to focus on helping caregivers, and its COVID-19 policies reviewed.
quote: The strategy should be examined to establish an efficient plan to support caregivers and their families.

title: Let CMS use HRSA's 340B data
proposal: The chapter says Congress should let CMS use the 340B drug program data HRSA collects instead of running its own survey, with penalties for not responding.
quote: Congress should allow CMS to use the 340B data that HRSA collects rather than having CMS conduct its own survey

title: Define telehealth location as where the provider is
proposal: The chapter says the law should treat a telehealth visit as happening where the provider is located, not where the patient is.
quote: Legally define the locus of service as where the provider is located during the telehealth visit rather than where the patient is.

title: Keep Trump-era religious exemptions to contraceptive mandate
proposal: The chapter says HHS should restore the Trump-era religious and moral exemptions to the ACA contraceptive mandate and rescind a 2023 proposed rule changing them if it becomes final.
quote: HHS should rescind, if finalized, the regulation titled “Coverage of Certain Preventive Services Under the Affordable Care Act,”

title: Issue women's preventive care mandate through public rulemaking
proposal: The chapter says HRSA should be required to reissue any women's preventive services coverage rules through the formal public notice and comment process.
quote: HRSA should be required to repromulgate any women’s preventive services mandates through the notice and comment process

title: End HRSA contracts with ACOG on preventive care
proposal: The chapter says HHS should end its contracts with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists to advise on the mandate and set up a new advisory committee under federal advisory committee law.
quote: HHS should rescind these contracts and establish an advisory committee that is compliant with the Federal Advisory Committee Act

title: Cover fertility awareness methods and supplies
proposal: The chapter says HRSA should issue rules following a court order and make sure fertility awareness-based family planning, including its supplies, is covered as women's preventive care.
quote: HHS should more thoroughly ensure that fertility awareness–based methods of family planning are part of women’s preventive services under the ACA.

title: Remove male condoms from women's preventive mandate
proposal: The chapter says HRSA should not include male-only contraceptive methods in women's preventive services guidelines.
quote: HRSA should not incorporate exclusively male contraceptive methods into guidelines that specify they encompass only women’s services.

title: Remove the drug Ella from the contraceptive mandate
proposal: The chapter says HRSA should remove the emergency contraceptive Ella (ulipristal acetate) from required coverage, calling it a potential abortifacient.
quote: woman’s uterus. HRSA should eliminate this potential abortifacient from the contraceptive mandate.

title: Withdraw Ryan White guidance on gender transition care
proposal: The chapter says HRSA should withdraw guidance encouraging Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program providers to offer gender transition care.
quote: HRSA should withdraw all guidance encouraging Ryan White HIV /AIDS Program service providers to provide controversial “gender transition” procedures

title: Keep federally funded medical training from covering abortion
proposal: The chapter says HHS should make sure training programs for doctors, nurses and doulas follow abortion funding limits and conscience laws.
quote: HHS should ensure that training programs for medical professionals—including doctors, nurses, and doulas—are in full compliance with restrictions on abortion funding

title: Enforce Coats-Snowe and make abortion training opt-in
proposal: The chapter says HHS should investigate medical schools' compliance with the Coats-Snowe Amendment, require states to ensure no mandatory abortion training, and tell medical schools abortion training must be opt-in.
quote: Communicate to medical schools that any abortion-related training must be on an opt-in rather than opt-out basis.

title: Fund home-based child care instead of universal day care
proposal: The chapter says that instead of universal day care, funding should go to parents to help them stay home with a child or pay for in-home care by family.
quote: Instead of providing universal day care, funding should go to parents either to offset the cost of staying home with a child or to pay for familial, in-home childcare.

title: Share resources on the mother-child relationship
proposal: The chapter says HRSA should provide information and relationship education on the importance of the mother-child bond.
quote: HRSA should provide resources and information on the importance of the mother–child relationship in child well-being.

title: Fund doula services for low-income mothers
proposal: The chapter says doulas should be an option for all mothers and the Maternal and Child Health program should work to fund them for low-income mothers.
quote: doulas should be an active option for all women whether they are giving birth in a traditional hospital, through midwifery, or at home.

title: Give Native patients more private care options outside IHS
proposal: The chapter says American Indian and Alaska Native patients should have better access to private health providers as alternatives to the Indian Health Service, possibly modeled on the VA MISSION Act.
quote: Patients in these populations should be empowered to rely on alternatives to IHS through better access to private health care providers.

title: Expand rural care through telehealth and interstate licensing
proposal: The chapter says HHS should cut regulations and encourage telehealth, interstate licensing (including for volunteers), and cheaper alternatives to hospitals in rural areas.
quote: Implement or encourage policies that increase the supply of health care providers, such as increased telehealth access and interstate licensure

title: Put time limits on public health emergencies
proposal: The chapter says Congress should set a time limit on public health emergency declarations and make the Secretary justify any extension.
quote: Congress should establish a set time frame for any PHE, placing on the Secretary the burden of proof as to why an extension of the PHE is necessary.

title: Write the HHS SUNSET rule into law
proposal: The chapter says Congress should make into law a reversed Trump-era rule requiring HHS agencies to review their regulations, which would expire if not reviewed.
quote: Congress should codify the now-reversed Trump Administration rule that required all HHS agencies to review regulations retrospectively and publish results

title: Investigate HHS role in COVID censorship and conscience violations
proposal: The chapter says HHS should investigate and fix any cases where it worked with tech companies to censor views during COVID or with advocates to violate conscience laws and the Hyde Amendment.
quote: Investigate, expose, and remediate any instances in which HHS violated people’ s rights by:

title: Replace reproductive health task force with a pro-life task force
proposal: The chapter says the Secretary should eliminate the HHS Reproductive Healthcare Access Task Force and create a pro-life task force.
quote: The Office of the Secretary should eliminate the HHS Repro-ductive Healthcare Access Task Force and install a pro-life task force

title: Restore "conception to natural death" in HHS mission
proposal: The chapter says HHS should reject the idea that abortion is health care and restore its mission statement to serve Americans "from conception to natural death."
quote: restoring its mission statement under the Strategic Plan and elsewhere to include furthering the health and well-being of all Americans

title: Create a Special Representative for Domestic Women's Health
proposal: The chapter says the next Administration should create a Special Representative for Domestic Women's Health to lead domestic policy on life and family issues.
quote: The next Administration should create a dedicated Special Representative for Domestic Women’s Health.

title: Keep sex separate from gender identity in HHS policy statements
proposal: The chapter says the Secretary's antidiscrimination statements should not treat sex as including gender identity or sexual orientation.
quote: The Secretary’s antidiscrimination policy statements should never conflate sex with gender identity or sexual orientation.

title: Restructure the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps
proposal: The chapter says the U.S. Public Health Service should be reorganized to be more like other uniformed services, with a simpler chain of command and a focus on quick deployments.
quote: The USPHS should be restructured to make it more like its sister uniformed services with a more streamlined chain of command

title: Merge the Assistant Secretary for Health and Surgeon General jobs
proposal: The chapter says the Assistant Secretary for Health and Surgeon General positions should be combined into one four-star Surgeon General, filled by a health care provider, with a three-star Deputy.
quote: The ASH and SG positions should be combined into one four-star position with the rank, responsibilities, and authority of the ASH retained

title: Withdraw HHS support for gender-affirming care
proposal: The chapter says the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health should withdraw all recommendations and support for gender transition treatments.
quote: The OASH should withdraw all recommendations of and support for cross-sex medical interventions and “gender-affirming care.”

title: Refocus Title X family planning on fertility awareness
proposal: The chapter says the Title X family planning program should focus more on fertility awareness education, and the program office should end religious discrimination in grants.
quote: The Title X family planning program should be reframed with a focus on better education around fertility awareness and holistic family planning

title: Reinstate Trump-era Title X rule separating abortion
proposal: The chapter says HHS should quickly rescind the 2021 Title X rule and reinstate the Trump-era rule requiring strict separation from abortion and not requiring abortion referrals.
quote: HHS should rescind the Biden Administration’s regulation and reinstate the Trump Administration regulation for the program.

title: Pass the Title X Abortion Provider Prohibition Act
proposal: The chapter says Congress should pass a law barring Title X family planning grants from going to groups that perform or fund abortions.
quote: passing legislation such as the Title X Abortion Provider Prohibition Act,78 which would prohibit family planning grants from going to entities that perform abortions

title: Review emergency roles of HHS preparedness office and FEMA
proposal: The chapter says the arrangement where FEMA takes control from HHS's preparedness office during declared emergencies should be reviewed for efficiency.
quote: arrange-ment should be reviewed—especially considering the COVID-19 pandemic—for improvements in efficiency according to expertise and available resources

title: Use the Defense Production Act only in gravest cases
proposal: The chapter says the President should use the Defense Production Act only in the most serious circumstances.
quote: The President should invoke the Defense Pro-duction Act,79 which is a form of temporary takeover of private enterprises, only in the gravest circumstances.

title: Make the national stockpile a supplier of last resort
proposal: The chapter says the Strategic National Stockpile should plan for supply chain disruptions and define itself as a last-resort supplier to governments, first responders and key medical staff.
quote: The SNS should clarify its mission as supplier of last resort to the federal government, state governments, or first responders and key medical staff

title: Rescind HHS PREP Act liability memo
proposal: The chapter says HHS lawyers should rescind a memo that suspended civil rights and other laws for pandemic countermeasures.
quote: Rescind its PREP Act liability memo. OGC issued a PREP Act liability memo that suspended application of civil rights and other laws

title: Return conscience and religious freedom enforcement to OCR
proposal: The chapter says memos and notices moving conscience and religious freedom enforcement from the Office for Civil Rights to the general counsel should be rescinded, restoring OCR's authority.
quote: Rescind efforts to curtail OCR authority over conscience and religious freedom.

title: Ask DOJ to repeal legal opinions on abortion funding and federal enclaves
proposal: The chapter says HHS lawyers should urge DOJ to repeal Office of Legal Counsel memos allowing abortion funding despite the Hyde Amendment and allowing abortions on federal enclaves.
quote: Encourage DOJ to repeal OLC memos allowing abortion funding despite Hyde and memos allowing federal enclave immunity to perform abortions

title: Rescind legal analysis behind COVID eviction moratorium
proposal: The chapter says HHS lawyers should rescind the legal analysis that allowed HHS to pause rental evictions during COVID.
quote: Rescind legal analysis that authorized HHS to impose a moratorium on rental evictions during COVID.

title: Rescind legal view limiting action on care for disabled newborns
proposal: The chapter says HHS lawyers should rescind an analysis saying a 1986 court case blocks HHS from acting on denial of care to newborns with disabilities.
quote: Rescind the OGC legal analysis saying that the injunction in Bowen v. American Hospital Association

title: Rescind analyses in Vermont nurse case and California funding
proposal: The chapter says HHS lawyers should rescind the analysis behind dropping a case about a nurse forced to take part in an abortion, and the analysis restoring $200 million in Medicaid funds to California.
quote: Rescind the legal analysis supporting the Biden Administration’ s decision to dismiss the University of Vermont Medical Center case

title: Upgrade global affairs director to Assistant Secretary
proposal: The chapter says the head of HHS's Office of Global Affairs should have the title of Assistant Secretary and lead the government's global health diplomacy.
quote: The Director of the Office of Global Affairs should have the title of Assistant Secretary

title: Give OGA oversight of the Mexico City policy
proposal: The chapter says the Office of Global Affairs should oversee carrying out the Mexico City policy across HHS and promote pro-life, pro-family priorities abroad.
quote: OGA should hold oversight authority for implementation of the Mexico City policy throughout all divisions.

title: Hold health attaches to Administration policy
proposal: The chapter says HHS health attaches abroad should be trained on Administration policy and replaced if their conduct goes against it.
quote: Health attachés in various global locations should be trained in the Administration’ s policies with clear expectations communicated

title: Restore and fully fund OCR's conscience division
proposal: The chapter says OCR should return to strong enforcement of conscience laws and restore and fully fund its Conscience and Religious Freedom Division with needed authority.
quote: It should restore and fully fund the Office of the Deputy Director for the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division (CRFD)

title: Cut funds to entities that violate conscience laws
proposal: The chapter says HHS should withdraw funding from groups that violate conscience laws and refuse to fix it, and make grant terms spell out these obligations.
quote: HHS should withdraw funding from any violating entities that refuse to correct their behavior

title: Finalize Trump-era OCR religious freedom rule
proposal: The chapter says a draft Trump-era rule setting out how OCR enforces the Religious Freedom Restoration Act should be issued and finalized.
quote: A draft OCR RFRA and religious freedom rule from the Trump Administration should be issued and finalized.

title: Restore religious exemption waivers for faith-based foster agencies
proposal: The chapter says HHS should bring back religious exemption waivers for child welfare agencies, especially faith-based adoption and foster care groups, and grant them to all who ask.
quote: HHS should reestablish waivers for state and child welfare agencies for religious exemptions, especially for faith-based adoption and foster care agencies.

title: Let OCR review religious objections to vaccines
proposal: The chapter says HHS should restore OCR's power to review religious accommodation requests from people who object to vaccines, including those made with fetal cell lines.
quote: HHS should restore OCR authority to review requests for and render opinions on the application of RFRA to requests for religious accommodation

title: Withdraw Biden-era guidance on gender identity under Section 1557
proposal: The chapter says OCR should remove all Biden-era guidance on sexual orientation and gender identity under Section 1557, including a 2022 statement about states' limits on youth gender treatments.
quote: Remove all guidance issued under the Biden Administration concerning sexual orientation and gender identity under Section 1557

title: Announce non-enforcement of gender identity protections
proposal: The chapter says OCR should state it will not enforce bans on sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination in the Section 1557 rule and will prioritize religious and conscience protections.
quote: Issue a general statement of policy specifying that it will not enforce any prohibition on sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination

title: Refocus civil rights enforcement on race, sex and disability cases
proposal: The chapter says OCR should focus Section 1557 enforcement on serious race, sex and disability cases, including claims against policies based on critical race theory and protections for infants born alive.
quote: Issue a general statement of policy announcing that it plans to enforce Section 1557 discrimination bans by refocusing on serious cases of race, sex, and disability discrimination.

title: Finalize disability rules on rationing and assisted suicide
proposal: The chapter says OCR should finalize Trump-era disability rules on crisis standards of care and Quality Adjusted Life Years, and a rule barring discriminatory assisted suicide and denial of care to disabled newborns.
quote: Issue and finalize the Trump-era draft disability rights regulations concerning crisis standards of care and use of Quality of Life Adjusted Years (QALYs)

title: Withdraw pharmacy guidance on abortion drugs
proposal: The chapter says OCR should withdraw its guidance on pharmacies' civil rights duties, which it says orders pharmacies to stock and dispense abortion drugs.
quote: OCR should withdraw its pharmacy abortion mandate guidance. OCR should withdraw its “Obligations Under Federal Civil Rights Laws to Ensure Access

title: Withdraw HIPAA privacy guidance on abortion
proposal: The chapter says OCR should withdraw its June 2022 HIPAA guidance on patient privacy and abortion after the Dobbs decision.
quote: OCR should withdraw its June 2022 guidance87 that purports to address patient privacy concerns following the Dobbs decision
